newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian oil pipeline closed by dynamite attack.
newsitem.headline: Colombian oil pipeline closed by dynamite attack.

text.p: Suspected leftist rebels blew up a section of Colombia's main oil pipeline, spilling about 5,000 barrels of crude and forcing it to suspend pumping for the first time this year, authorities said on Wednesday.

A spokesman for the state oil company Ecopetrol said the attack on the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline occurred on Tuesday afternoon in a remote area of Arauca province, about 200 miles (320 km) northeast of Bogota.

Repair work was under way and pumping was expected to resume early on Thursday, he said, adding that National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas were believed to be responsible for setting the dynamite charge.

State security police (DAS) arrested four ELN commandos in the main oil production centre of Barrancabermeja. The four, including a 32-year-old woman identified as Luisa Viviana Madera, are suspected of carrying out a string of attacks on the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline over the past four years.
They were also being investigated for their possible links to the killing of a senior DAS official in Barrancabermeja in March 1996, a security police statement said.
The ELN, founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, specialises in economic sabotage and attacks on oil and coal projects across Colombia.
The Cano-Limon-Covenas pipeline carries about 200,000 barrels a day of crude from the Cano Limon field operated by Occidental Petroleum to the Covenas oil terminal on the Caribbean coast.
It was blown up 47 times in 1996 in attacks that spilled more than 100,000 barrels of crude and cost over $9 million in environmental damage and repairs, according to Ecopetrol.
